objectives: Name the food classes, their sources and uses.
Describe the path of food through the digestive system.

reviewNotes: Energy values (17 and 37 kJ/g) are the standard rounded figures; check which the syllabus prefers. Dietary and dental advice is general and to be reviewed by a health worker.

blocks.title: Food classes
blocks.md:
- **Carbohydrates** (cassava, yam, rice, plantain): energy.
- **Proteins** (beans, fish, eggs, meat): growth and repair.
- **Fats and oils** (palm oil, groundnuts): energy store; fat gives about 37 kJ per g against about 17 kJ per g for carbohydrate.
- **Vitamins and minerals** (fruit, vegetables, green leaves such as eru): health.
- **Fibre**: helps food pass through the gut.
- **Water**: needed by all cells.

blocks.caption: The digestive system: path of food.
blocks.alt: Five boxes joined by arrows: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine and large intestine, each with its main job.

blocks.title: Digestion
blocks.md: **Digestion** breaks large insoluble food molecules into small soluble ones using **enzymes** (and in the stomach, acid). The small molecules are **absorbed** through the wall of the **small intestine** into the blood. In the large intestine **water** is absorbed; undigested waste leaves as faeces. A **balanced diet** contains all the food classes in the right amounts.

blocks.title: Teeth and care
blocks.md: Adults have 32 teeth: **incisors** (cutting), **canines** (tearing), **premolars and molars** (grinding). Tooth decay happens when bacteria use sugar to make **acid** that attacks the enamel. Brush twice a day, avoid sugary snacks between meals, and see a dentist or health worker if you have toothache.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Most absorption of food happens in the small intestine, not in the stomach.
- Digestion is not the same as absorption: digestion breaks food down; absorption moves it into the blood.
- A balanced diet is not the same for everyone: it depends on age and activity.

blocks.title: Energy from fats and carbohydrates
blocks.statement: Use 37 kJ per g for fat and 17 kJ per g for carbohydrate. Find the energy in 10 g of each.

blocks.title: Order the organs
blocks.statement: Put in order: stomach, mouth, large intestine, small intestine, gullet.
steps: Food is chewed in the mouth and swallowed down the gullet.
Then: stomach, small intestine, large intestine.
blocks.answer: mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine

objectives: Describe the path of air to the lungs and gas exchange.

reviewNotes: Exhaled-air composition (about 16 % O₂, 4 % CO₂) and resting pulse range are standard textbook approximations; check the figures used in class.

blocks.title: Breathing and gas exchange
blocks.md: Air passes through the **nose**, **windpipe (trachea)** and **bronchi** to tiny air sacs called **alveoli** in the **lungs**. There **oxygen** passes into the blood and **carbon dioxide** passes out. To breathe in, the ribs move **up and out** and the **diaphragm flattens**, so the chest becomes larger and air enters. To breathe out, they relax and air leaves.

blocks.caption: Approximate percentage of oxygen and carbon dioxide in inhaled (in) and exhaled (out) air.
blocks.alt: A bar chart: oxygen in 21, oxygen out 16, carbon dioxide in 0.04, carbon dioxide out 4 (percent).

blocks.title: Blood
blocks.md: **Blood** is a transport tissue. **Red blood cells** carry oxygen (they contain haemoglobin). **White blood cells** fight germs. **Platelets** help blood to clot. **Plasma**, the liquid part, carries digested food, carbon dioxide, wastes and hormones. Heat is also carried around the body.

blocks.title: Heart and vessels
blocks.md: The **heart** is a muscular pump with four chambers. **Arteries** carry blood **away** from the heart (thick walls); **veins** carry blood **to** the heart (valves stop backflow); **capillaries** are tiny vessels where exchange with cells happens. The **pulse** shows the heart rate. At rest an adult heart beats roughly 60 to 100 times a minute.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- The body uses only part of the oxygen we breathe in: exhaled air still contains about 16 % oxygen.
- Breathing (moving air) is not respiration (releasing energy in cells).
- Veins do not all carry blue blood; the colour is always some red.
